dish: Okinawa zenzai (brown-sugar-simmered beans under a mound of shaved ice)
n: Sennichi (千日)
w: Naha's classic zenzai parlour near Naminoue Shrine, in business since the 1950s (the founders' Yafune Shokudo, then 'Sennichi' in Kume from 1962). Order the Okinawa zenzai: plump, slow-stewed beans under a triangle of hand-shaved ice.

dish: Frosted-mug root beer and curly fries
n: A&W Makiminato (A&W 牧港店)
w: A&W came to Okinawa in 1963, years before mainland Japan — the 24-hour Makiminato drive-in on Route 58 is the chain's Okinawa flagship. Root beer in a frosted mug, curly fries and a burger is a rite of passage.

dish: American-size sirloin / tenderloin steak (Ishigaki-beef option)
n: Steakhouse 88 Tsuji Honten (ステーキハウス88 辻本店)
w: Flagship of the Steakhouse 88 chain, descended from 'CLUB88', an A-sign restaurant licensed for US personnel in 1955. Neon diner room, 20-plus steak cuts, open till 1 am — the classic Okinawan 'shime' (end-of-night) steak.

dish: Sanmainiku soba and aasa (sea-lettuce) soba with house-made noodles
n: Nakamura Soba (なかむらそば)
w: Roadside soba house near Manza Beach: preservative-free house noodles, a light but bonito-rich broth and pork belly that falls apart at a touch; the aasa soba works sea lettuce into both noodles and topping.

dish: Okinawa soba (modern, clear-broth style)
n: OKINAWA SOBA EIBUN
w: A newer-generation Naha soba shop that made both the Okinawa Times 900-reader noodle poll and Okinawa Traveler's five soba shops locals recommend with confidence.

dish: Okinawa soba in three noodles (classic, soy-milk, seaweed) with bonito broth
n: Yagiya (屋宜家)
address: 1172 Ōgan, Yaese, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
w: Soba served in a registered cultural-property red-tiled house; choose classic, soy-milk or seaweed noodles in a light but deep bonito broth.

dish: Okinawa soba
n: Nanbu Soba (南部そば)
address: Southern Okinawa main island, Okinawa, Japan
w: Southern soba shop picked both in the Okinawa Times 2023 noodle-lovers' poll (south edition) and by Okinawa Traveler's locals-recommend five.

dish: Soki soba in a 100-year-old house
n: Ufuya (百年古家 大家)
w: A century-old Okinawan farmhouse compound in the hills above Nago serving soki soba and agu pork; one of Okinawa Traveler's locals-recommend five and on Stars and Stripes' soba trail.

dish: Zenzai (brown-sugar kintoki beans under shaved ice)
n: Arakaki Zenzai-ya (新垣ぜんざい屋)
w: Motobu's half-century-old zenzai shop that does exactly one thing: sweet stewed red kidney beans buried under a peak of shaved ice, bought with a ticket from the door.

dish: Okinawa soba and Ryukyu home cooking
n: Shima-jikan, Onna (沖縄料理の店 島時間)
w: Onna village Okinawan kitchen certified by Okinawa Prefecture as a 'restaurant where you can taste Ryukyu cuisine' and picked in Okinawa Traveler's soba round-up.

dish: Miyako-miso champuru and rafute
n: Inaka Ryōri no Mise Kura, Miyako (田舎料理の店 蔵)
w: Country-cooking izakaya in Hirara using island miso in champuru and rafute; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine and a Mapple guidebook pick.

dish: Duru-ten (taro croquette, invented here) with awamori from every distillery
n: Urizun (古酒と琉球料理 うりずん)
w: Opened 15 August 1972 by gathering bottles from every awamori distillery in Okinawa — the bar that brought awamori back to the people. Order duru-ten, the fried taro croquette Okinawa Times traces to this kitchen, and a flight of kūsu (aged awamori).

dish: Miyako soba in a bonito-forward broth
n: Irabu Soba Kame (伊良部そば かめ)
w: Irabu Island's soba stop, where the bonito hits you first; reached over the Irabu Bridge and named in both Okinawa Times' Miyako soba coverage and Mapple's Miyako-soba top ten.

dish: Soki Miyako soba with a garlicky pork-bone broth
n: Maruyoshi Shokudō (丸吉食堂)
w: Out in Gusukube, a family shokudō serving the owner's mother's Miyako soba: pork-bone broth perfumed with garlic and big soki ribs.

dish: Old-style Miyako soba
n: Yamato Shokudō (大和食堂)
w: Hirara regulars' shop serving the same plain, honest Miyako soba for some forty years.

dish: Aosa-kneaded noodles in bonito-trimmings broth
n: Minato Shokudō, Miyako (みなと食堂)
w: Harbour-side shokudō near Sunayama whose house noodles are kneaded with aosa seaweed and served in a broth from bonito trimmings — a taste found only here.

dish: Miyako soba straight from the noodle maker
n: Jinku-ya (じんく屋)
w: Counter run by Kusamatsu Seimen, one of Miyako's two big noodle makers: chewy fresh noodles, simple bonito soup.

dish: Ishigaki-beef yakiniku from a whole-animal buy
n: Ishigaki-gyū Sumibi Yakiniku Yamamoto (石垣牛 炭火焼肉 やまもと)
w: The Ishigaki-beef yakiniku house locals queue for: buying whole animals means rare cuts on the board, grilled over charcoal; opens at 17:00 and closes when the meat runs out.

dish: Island-raised kuroge wagyu (Ishigaki beef) yakiniku
n: Shima no Ushi Ishigaki-ya (島のうし 石垣屋)
w: A more polished Ishigaki-beef room with private booths, picked by both of Japan's big guidebook series for island black wagyu.

dish: Miso Yaeyama soba
n: Kimi Shokudō, Ishigaki (キミ食堂)
w: Ishigaki town shokudō famous for its miso-broth take on Yaeyama soba — a noodle-lovers' poll pick and one of Rurubu's 'creative' soba bowls.

dish: Yaeyama soba with a well-built dashi
n: Shiraho Shokudō (白保食堂)
w: Village shokudō in Shiraho on Ishigaki's east coast with a long menu from island dishes to yōshoku; the Yaeyama soba is the best seller.

dish: Rafute, champuru and awamori in an old-house izakaya
n: Dachibin Naha Kumoji (沖縄居酒屋 抱瓶 那覇久茂地店)
w: The Naha outpost of an Okinawan izakaya that made its name in Tokyo, in a Shōwa-era wooden house; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine.

dish: Orion Draft fresh from the plant (factory tour + tasting)
n: Orion Happy Park — Orion Beer Nago Brewery (オリオンハッピーパーク)
w: Okinawa's own beer since 1957: the Nago plant's tour ends with a tasting of just-brewed Orion Draft; shop, restaurant and a small history gallery.

dish: House-brewed lager, weizen, pale ale, IPA and stout
n: Chatan Harbor Brewery & Restaurant (チャタンハーバーブルワリー)
w: Seafront brewpub a few minutes from American Village brewing five year-round beers on site, with a terrace over the East China Sea at sunset.

dish: Cask-aged awamori kūsu 'Kura' and Helios craft beer
n: Helios Distillery (ヘリオス酒造)
w: Founded as a rum distiller in 1961 and brewing Okinawa's pioneering craft beer since 1996; the free tour shows 2,600 barrels of aging awamori stacked to the roof.

dish: Okinawan tempura (fish, squid, mozuku) from ¥100 a piece
n: Ganso Nakamoto Tempura, Ōjima (元祖中本てんぷら店)
w: The queue-every-day tempura stand facing Ōjima fishing port, attached to a fish shop: thick-battered Okinawan tempura of fish, squid, mozuku seaweed and vegetables, eaten hot by the sea.

dish: 'Evolved' taco rice with aburi soki and three cheeses
n: Tomigusuku Taco Rice (豊見城タコライス)
w: A new-wave taco rice: spiced meat, three cheeses, corn tortilla and a torched soki rib on top.

dish: Kumejima deep-sea-water kuruma prawns, umibudō and Kumejima red chicken
n: Nantō Shokurakuen, Kume Island (南島食楽園)
w: Big open izakaya by Eef Beach built around Kume's own produce: kuruma prawns raised in deep-ocean water, sea grapes, island red chicken, grouper and octopus, from Okinawan plates to nigiri.

dish: Island kamaboko (kuruma-prawn, mozuku and squid-ink fish cakes)
n: Sukeroku Kamaboko, Kume Island (助ろく)
w: Kume's fish-cake maker, carrying on a 60-year-old craft: chewy island kamaboko flavoured with kuruma prawn, mozuku or squid ink — a classic island snack.

dish: Yaeyama soba with pipātsu (island long-pepper)
n: Sobadokoro Takenoko, Taketomi (そば処 竹の子)
address: Taketomi Village, Taketomi Island, Okinawa, Japan
w: Taketomi's most popular eating house, around forty years old, ladling the previous generation's Yaeyama soba in the red-tile village.

dish: Hand-drip single-origin pour-over roasted in-house
n: Tamagusuku Coffee Roasters (タマグスクコーヒー)
w: Ten-seat roaster-café off Kokusai-dōri often called the island's best cup: the owner asks what you like, then drips light-to-dark single origins one cup at a time.

dish: Deep-roast iced coffee from a yatai cart
n: Coffee Yatai Hibari-ya (珈琲屋台 ひばり屋)
w: An open-air coffee stall tucked into a leafy back alley near Makishi Station — ground-to-order hand drip and a famous deep-roast iced coffee on mismatched chairs.

dish: Morning pour-over from 6 am
n: rokkan COFFEE SHURI (ロッカン コーヒー シュリ)
w: Second shop (Oct 2023) of Naha roaster rokkan COFFEE CREATORS, opening at 6 am near Shuri Castle — a 'sixth sense' coffee before the castle crowds.

dish: Mexican-style tacos with spices imported from Mexico
n: Tacos Café Tacoloco, Chatan (タコスカフェ タコロコ)
w: American Village taquería making properly Mexican tacos — spices shipped from Mexico — a counterpoint to Okinawa's crunchy-shell post-war tacos.

dish: Pick-your-own kaisendon, gurukun and island-fish sashimi
n: Itoman Fishermen's Co-op Osakana Center, Michi-no-Eki Itoman (糸満漁協 お魚センター)
w: Eleven fishmongers run by the Itoman fishermen's co-op inside Japan's southernmost roadside station: choose fish for a kaisendon, nigiri, fish soup or Okinawan tempura and eat on the spot, 10:00–19:00.

dish: Fūchibā (mugwort) soba with house-made noodles
n: Mendokoro Tiandaa (麺処 てぃあんだー)
w: Cult Naha soba shop known for house-made noodles; the fūchibā soba arrives fragrant with Okinawan mugwort. In both Okinawa Traveler's soba feature and Mapple's Okinawa-soba round-up.

dish: Tebichi (slow-braised pig's trotter) soba
n: Sobaya Yoshiko, Motobu (そば屋よしこ)
w: One of the stars of Motobu's 'soba highway' (Prefectural Route 84, 20-plus soba shops): come for the meltingly braised tebichi on a pork-bonito-kombu broth.

dish: Teppanyaki steak cooked tableside
n: Teppanyaki Steak House Shiki, Sonoda Honten (ステーキハウス四季 園田本店)
w: A Koza teppanyaki steak house running for close to half a century in the post-war steak heartland by Kadena; chefs sear the steak on the iron in front of you.

dish: A-lunch (Okinawan diner combo plate) and Ryukyu dishes
n: Kaizoku Kōbō, Okinawa Zoo & Museum (こどもの国レストラン 海族工房)
address: Okinawa Zoo & Museum (Okinawa Kodomo no Kuni), Okinawa City, Okinawa, Japan
w: The zoo's ground-floor restaurant is no afterthought: prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine and picked by Okinawa City's tourism portal for its 'A-lunch', the post-war diner combo plate.

dish: Special Lunch / A-lunch diner plate and steak
n: Highway Drive-In Restaurant, Okinawa City (ハイウェイ食堂)
w: Opened in 1972 by a US Army cook as an A-sign establishment and seemingly frozen in time since: huge diner plates, low prices, fast service, open till 2 am on Route 75.

dish: Beni-imo (purple sweet potato) and salt-chinsukō ice cream
n: Blue Seal Makiminato Honten (ブルーシール 牧港本店)
w: 'Born in America, raised in Okinawa': Blue Seal started in 1948 supplying the US bases and moved to this Makiminato drive-in in 1963. The flagship was rebuilt and reopened in 2024 to a 400-person queue — order beni-imo or salt-chinsukō.

dish: Ryu-pin 'Ice Mountain' tropical-fruit shaved ice and eight kinds of sata andagi
n: Onna no Eki Nakayukui Ichiba (おんなの駅 なかゆくい市場)
w: West-coast roadside market that every drive north stops at: island produce, snack stalls frying sata andagi (brown sugar, beni-imo and more), and Ryu-pin's mountainous tropical-fruit kakigōri.

dish: Okinawan tempura (fish, squid, mozuku, red ginger) at ¥80 a piece
n: Michi-no-Eki Kyoda — Yanbaru Bussan Center (道の駅許田)
w: The roadside station at the end of the Okinawa Expressway, gateway to Yanbaru: produce from the twelve northern towns and a takeout row famous for hot Okinawan tempura and tacos. Renewed in 2021.

dish: Miyako awamori with island dishes and live sanshin
n: Awamori to Okinawa Ryōri Gōya, Miyako (泡盛と沖縄料理 郷家)
w: Hirara's classic shimauta izakaya: Miyako's own awamori brands, island home cooking, and nightly sanshin folk-song sets that end with the whole room dancing kachāshī.

dish: Miyako-mango and island-fruit gelato (about 30 flavours)
n: RICCO gelato, Miyako (リッコジェラート)
w: Italian-trained gelato maker in Hirara churning Miyako's own mangoes, fruits and even island salt and vegetables into some thirty flavours.

dish: Island-ingredient lunch plates and fruit-laden sweets with a sea view
n: Shima Café Tunkaraya, Miyako (島cafe とぅんからや)
w: Hilltop café in southern Miyako looking over the sea, cooking 'made in Miyako' lunches and fruit-heavy desserts.

dish: Fresh-milk gelato from the farm's own cows, with a sea view
n: Ishigaki-jima Milmil Honpo (石垣島ミルミル本舗)
w: Dairy-farm gelato stand on a hill above the sea west of Ishigaki town; the plain milk flavour is the best seller. Open until sunset.

dish: Hand-made gyōza and Chinese small plates with Orion
n: Benriya Yulinglong, Sakaemachi (べんり屋 玉玲瓏)
w: The pioneer of Sakaemachi market's night drinking: when the stalls shutter, tables fill the alley for its hand-made gyōza. Both Rurubu and Mapple name it first among the market's after-dark haunts.

dish: Island-fish sashimi and nitsuke with awamori
n: Nakamura-ya, Kumoji (海産物料理とあわもりの店 なかむら家)
w: Seafood-and-awamori izakaya in Kumoji where regulars come for whatever the boats brought in — island fish sashimi and simmered fish, washed down with awamori.

dish: Awamori from every distillery and kūsu aged 3 to 30+ years, poured by awamori sommeliers
n: Karakara to Chibugwā (カラカラとちぶぐゎ〜)
address: Yamako 2nd Bldg 1F, 3-15-15 Kumoji, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
w: Naha's awamori-specialist bar: bottles from every distillery in the prefecture and aged kūsu past thirty years, with three awamori sommeliers to steer you; prefecture-certified for Ryukyu cuisine.

dish: Old-and-new Okinawan small plates with awamori
n: Kozakura (小桜)
w: A seventy-year-old koryōriya off Kokusai-dōri, believed to be the oldest surviving restaurant of its era in Naha; the third-generation owner keeps both old and new Okinawan dishes on the menu.

dish: Seasonal jewel-box fruit tarts
n: oHacorté Minatogawa Honten (オハコルテ 港川本店)
w: The fruit-tart shop (founded 2009) that made Minatogawa's 'Stateside Town' — some thirty shops and cafés in converted 1950s US military housing — a destination; glossy seasonal tarts in a little white house.

dish: Island-vegetable lunch plates in a hillside forest garden
n: Yama no Chaya Rakusui, Nanjō (山の茶屋 楽水)
w: A café built into the rock above Hyakuna beach, sister to Hamabe no Chaya below — slow island lunches with a sea view through the trees.

dish: House-made pizza unchanged for 25 years, with a view to Ie and Sesoko islands
n: Pizza Kissa Kajinhō, Motobu (ピザ喫茶 花人逢)
w: Red-tiled old-house café on a hilltop above Motobu serving the same home-made pizza for a quarter-century; on clear days Ie-jima, Sesoko and Minna float on the horizon.

dish: Coffee and zenzai among 100 shīsā in a jungle garden
n: Yachimun Kissa Shīsā-en, Motobu (やちむん喫茶 シーサー園)
w: A red-roofed Okinawan farmhouse swallowed by subtropical forest, with more than a hundred local potters' shīsā lions perched on roofs and walls around the tables.

dish: Lunch plates and home-made cakes
n: Cafe ichara, Motobu (カフェ イチャラ)
w: A Motobu forest café picked by Rurubu, Mapple and Okinawa Traveler's 'sea or forest?' round-up of northern cafés.

dish: Sea-view lunch and cake above Hyakuna beach
n: Cafe Yabusachi, Nanjō (カフェ やぶさち)
w: Glass-fronted café on the Nanjō coast looking straight out over the Pacific — part of the trio of southern sea-view cafés with Hamabe no Chaya and Rakusui.

dish: Adan-sprout champuru, mozuku tempura and garlic-fried umuzuna
n: Shima Ryōri Izakaya Adan-tei, Ishigaki (島料理居酒屋 あだん亭)
w: Ishigaki town izakaya cooking genuinely Yaeyaman dishes from island produce — try the champuru of adan (screw-pine) shoots — and the only Yaeyama restaurant on the prefecture's Ryukyu-cuisine certified list.

dish: Kunigami donuts, Oku green tea and karagi (cinnamon-leaf) tea
n: Michi-no-Eki Yuiyui Kunigami (道の駅 ゆいゆい国頭)
w: The Yanbaru roadside station that gathers Kunigami village's food: Oku-grown green tea, karagi tea and the local Kunigami doughnuts — the last big food stop before Cape Hedo.

dish: Tomigusuku mango sweets and produce
n: Michi-no-Eki Toyosaki (道の駅 豊崎)
w: The roadside station closest to Naha Airport, stocked with Tomigusuku's mango products and island produce — a last-stop for food souvenirs.

dish: Classic Okinawa soba
n: Takaesu Soba, Urasoe (高江洲そば)
w: An Urasoe institution counted among the 'traditional royal-road' soba shops by Rurubu and voted into the Okinawa Times noodle-lovers' central-region list.

dish: Okinawa soba
n: Kingetsu Soba Yomitan Honten (金月そば 読谷本店)
w: Yomitan soba house on both Okinawa Traveler's area-by-area soba list and Rurubu's 16 best Okinawa-soba shops.

dish: Okinawa soba
n: Sachichan Soba (幸っちゃんそば)
w: A northern soba shop picked in the Okinawa Times 2023 noodle-lovers' poll (north edition) and Rurubu's 16 'famous & characterful' soba shops.

dish: Okinawa soba and house-grown herb tea in a registered-heritage house
n: Chadokoro Makabe Chinā, Itoman (茶処 真壁ちなー)
w: Soba and herb tea served in a red-tiled, stone-walled homestead whose house and grounds are a national Registered Tangible Cultural Property — the old southern-village Okinawa landscape intact.

dish: C-lunch (heaped diner combo plate) — about half of all orders
n: Keishoku no Mise Ruby, Tomari (軽食の店ルビー)
w: Sixty-plus-year-old Tomari diner whose name belies mountainous portions: some 80 dishes from champuru to loco moco, but half the room orders the C-lunch. Namie Amuro used to drop in after dance practice.

dish: Pork-tamago and 100-plus shokudō dishes (historic)
n: Ayagu Shokudō, Shuri — CLOSED
w: Shuri's 'tasty, fast, cheap' shokudō, opened 1979 with a menu that once topped 100 dishes, closed at the end of October 2023 after 44 years when rising costs made it unsustainable. Kept on the map as a closed landmark of Okinawan shokudō culture — do not travel for it.

dish: 24-hour Okinawan shokudō plates (historic)
n: Ichigin Shokudō, Kumoji — CLOSED
w: Downtown Naha's 24-hour Okinawan diner, a C-lunch favourite, closed on 23 January after staff shortages and soaring costs (Okinawa Times). Listed as closed — do not travel for it.

dish: 80-plus shokudō dishes, from champuru to curry, in student portions
n: Yanbaru Shokudō, Naha (やんばる食堂)
address: In front of Okinawa University, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
w: Opened 1974 opposite Okinawa University and still feeding students from a menu of more than eighty dishes — an Okinawan 'mother's cooking' shokudō in both Rurubu's and Okinawa Traveler's local-diner picks.

dish: Home-style Okinawan teishoku cooked by the anmā (mothers) of the kitchen
n: Oshokujidokoro Mikado, Naha (お食事処 みかど)
w: A Route 58 shokudō where Okinawan mothers cook the island's everyday dishes — champuru, soups, chanpon rice — fast and cheap.

dish: Yushi-dōfu (fresh-curd island tofu) from the factory next door
n: Kaiyō Shokudō, Tomigusuku (海洋食堂)
w: Tomigusuku shokudō famous for yushi-dōfu, soft just-made island tofu carried over from the adjoining tofu works and served in soup or soba.

dish: Island vegetables, seafood and Ishigaki beef with 45-plus house fruit & herb liqueurs
n: Mori no Kenja, Ishigaki (森の賢者)
w: Small Ishigaki-town kitchen cooking island vegetables, fish and Ishigaki beef without chemical seasonings, with awamori, sake and more than 45 home-made fruit and herb liqueurs; book ahead.

dish: Fresh Yaeyama tuna — sashimi platters, tuna cutlet and seared toro
n: Maguro Senmon Izakaya Hitoshi, Ishigantō (まぐろ専門居酒屋 ひとし 石敢當店)
w: Ishigaki's famous tuna izakaya, packed with locals and visitors alike for heaped plates of just-landed island tuna; book or queue at 16:30.

dish: Irabu (sea-snake) soup, gazami mud-crab pasta and Ryukyu wild-boar soup
n: KITCHEN inaba, Iriomote (キッチン イナバ)
address: 742-6 Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
w: Iriomote's island-food kitchen near Uehara port: rare local ingredients — irabu sea-snake soup, gazami crab, Ryukyu wild boar in season — alongside traditional and Western-style plates, with jungle-green mountains in the windows.

dish: Grilled crab, sashimi salad and grouper simmered in island salt (māsu-ni)
n: Shima Gourmet ROCO, Iriomote (島ぐるめ ROCO)
address: 58 Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
w: Uehara dining room cooking Iriomote's sea and mountain catch — grilled crab, sashimi salad, squid-ink rice croquettes and grouper simmered in island salt.

dish: Soki soba and taco rice with a view down the sea causeway
n: Umi-no-Eki Ayahashi-kan, Kaichū-dōro (海の駅 あやはし館)
w: The 'sea station' halfway along the 5 km Kaichū-dōro causeway: local produce and the Kaichū Chaya restaurant upstairs serving soki soba and taco rice over the shallows.

dish: Nuchi Māsu mineral sea salt (and salt soft-serve) with a free factory tour
n: Nuchi Māsu Salt Factory, Miyagi Island (ぬちまーす観光製塩ファクトリー)
w: Clifftop salt works across the Kaichū-dōro on Miyagi Island, where a patented spray-drying method snows mineral-rich salt inside the factory; free 10-minute tours every 20 minutes, a sea-view restaurant and shop.

dish: Free awamori tasting at a distillery founded in 1883
n: Awamori Masahiro Gallery, Itoman (泡盛まさひろギャラリー)
w: Gallery-shop of Masahiro Distillery (founded 1883): watch the production line through glass, browse displays on awamori's history and taste for free.

dish: Suppaiman dried salted plums and plum candy, made in front of you
n: Uema Kashiten Factory — Suppaiman (上間菓子店 工場見学)
w: Free factory tour of the maker of Suppaiman, Okinawa's cult dried-plum snack and its mascot; watch the plums and candies being made (video only on Saturdays).

dish: Mozuku champuru, home-made jīmāmi (peanut) tofu and Zamami-caught set meals
n: Restaurant Marumi-ya, Zamami (レストラン まるみ屋)
address: Zamami village, Zamami Island, Okinawa, Japan
w: Five minutes from Zamami port: hearty daily set lunches built on island produce — mozuku seaweed champuru and house-made jīmāmi peanut tofu are the favourites.

dish: A-lunch at noon, island izakaya plates and karaoke at night
n: Karaoke Izakaya Marine Box, Tokashiki (カラオケ居酒屋マリンボックス)
w: The port-side all-rounder of Tokashiki village: an A-lunch plate at midday, then island izakaya dishes and karaoke until midnight.
